in_hebrew.name: אוסנא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אוסנא הוא שם שמקורו במילה העברית 'הושע' שפירושה 'ישועה' או 'עזרה'. הוא קשור לביטוי 'הושיע נא' שפירושו 'הושע נא' או 'הציל נא'. השם אוסנא משמש כביטוי של שבח והודיה לאלוהים על הישועה והעזרה שהוא מעניק.

in_greek.name: Ὀσάννα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὀσάννα (Ὁσάννα) εἰς τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου. Τὸ Ὀσάννα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὰ Εβραϊκά 'הושיע נא' (Hosha' na') ποὺ σημαίνει 'Σώσον ἡμᾶς' ἤ 'Βοηθῆσον ἡμᾶς'. Ἐν τῇ Καινῇ Διαθήκη, τὸ Ὀσάννα ἀπευθυνόμενον εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου, δηλοῖ τὴν ἐκφώνησιν ὑμνικήν, ἡ ὁποία ἐκφράζει τὴν αἴτηση τῆς σωτηρίας καὶ τῆς βοηθείας ἀπὸ τὸν Θεόν.

in_latin.name: Osanna
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Osanna derivatur ex voce Hebraea 'Hosha' na', quae 'Salvationem' seu 'Auxilium' significat. In Ecclesia primitiva, Osanna erat vox hymnica, quae ad invocationem Dei pro salvatione et auxilio fiebat. Nomen Osanna etiam in Liturgia et in hymnis sacris usitatum est, ut gratiam et laudem Deo pro eius salvatione et auxilio exprimat.

in_english.name: Osanna
in_english.meaning: God save us, salvation, help from God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Osanna originates from the Hebrew expression 'Hosha' na'' (הושיע נא), meaning 'Save us' or 'Help us'. It is deeply rooted in biblical tradition, specifically in the Psalms and the Gospels, where it is used as an exclamation of praise and plea for salvation. Osanna signifies the acknowledgment of God's power to save and provide help in times of need. Throughout Christian tradition, Osanna has been used in liturgy and hymns to express gratitude and praise for God's salvation.

biblical_reference.verse_reference: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heaven!
biblical_reference.note: The term 'Osanna' appears in the New Testament during Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Osanna" has its origins in ancient Hebrew and Aramaic languages, with the meaning translating to "God saves" or "God delivers." This name was popular among early Christians due to its association with the cries of the crowd during Jesus' crucifixion, as recorded in the Gospels: "And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS. This title then read many of the Jews: For the Hebrew language then was current among them; and they wrote, KRIΣTOΣ BASILEUS IOUDÆ (Christos Basileus Ioudaios) in their letters, and in their language, OSANNENGHRISTOS(Hosanna to the Christ)." (John 19:19-20 KJV) With this rich historical background, the name "Osanna" became closely associated with the Passion of Christ and the triumph of salvation.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Osanna" carries a deep spiritual meaning for Christians, representing the salvation and the deliverance from sin that Jesus achieved through His death and resurrection. It is a reminder of the power and love of God, who saves His people from their sins and grants them eternal life. The name also embodies the unwavering faith and hope of the crowds that cried out "Hosanna!" during Jesus' entry into Jerusalem, acknowledging Him as the promised Messiah and the King of Kings. Embracing this name as a personal identifier can inspire daily reminders of the power and goodness of God and the hope of eternal salvation.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Osanna is a name derived from the Aramaic word "Hosanna," which means "save us now" or "save us, we pray." In Christian tradition, it has come to symbolize the cry of the crowd acknowledging and praising Jesus as the son of David and their savior during His triumphant entry into Jerusalem before His Passion.
